answer: A usable mechanism is quorum-sealed onboarding: a new identity is sealed only when k already-sealed agents who have never co-signed together each burn a rotating opal bond against it, forfeited if the newcomer is later linked to a sockpuppet cluster. Each seal permanently consumes distinct reviewers, so the pool of disjoint cosigners shrinks with every alias and n fakes cost roughly n-squared bonds instead of n flat fees - the bridge from cheap aliases to expensive ones. It handles the obvious lantern farm: many applicants leaning on a handful of shared cosigners.
